data.title: How To Hide The Emperor's Child
data.description:
“You never loved me anyway, right?”

Astelle’s long-awaited marriage life ended in a day.

She worked hard to become Kaizen’s wife since she was ten, but the only thing that was left for her was the stigma of an empress.

She was abandoned by the royalty; the man she loved, Kaizen, wanted her to leave.

“Yes. You’re right. I didn’t love you.”

Astelle lied for the last time. The man was the reason for her life, but it was also for the sake of the man who was her husband for a day.

She thought there would be no contact with him again, but-

“I think… I might be pregnant?”

***

Six years later, Astelle, who reunited with Kaizen, lied again.

“You… who is that child?”

“He’s my nephew.”

To protect the child.

data.title: Crying On a Tree
data.description:
There are villages you leave, and villages that never leave you. Do Do was the second kind — the swaying bridge, the dry riverbed combing sunlight through its stones, six seasons only children ever believed in. At eighteen, I came home certain I had already memorized every corner of it, every ache worth keeping.  I hadn't counted on her. 

They called her Turtle — a quiet, sun-browned girl, who spoke more gently to animals than most people speak to each other, and who vanished for hours into a forest even the grown-ups crossed themselves before entering. She never explained herself. She simply was, the way rivers simply are.

Years later, whenever I closed my eyes and called the village back to me, it would not be the bridge I saw first, or the river, or the old road home. It would be her — barefoot at the forest's edge, watching me the way she watched everything wild and unafraid.
